Sperm Ca2+ ATP-ase activity is not mediated by SERCAs, but by a secretory pathway Ca-ATPase, which we have termed SPCA1.

(1), the sperm-specific Ca2+ pump SPCA1 is responsible for the regulation of [Ca2+ ]i in human spermatozoon; (2) SERCAs do not play a role in the Ca2+ regulation in human spermatoza; (3) SPCA1 is localized in the area behind the nucleus in spermatozoa; (4) the SPCA1 is the main Ca2+ pump responsible for [Ca2+]i regulation in
the SERCA inhibitors thapsigargins (0.1–1 μM) cyclopiazonic (10 μM) acid failed to affect resting and progesterone-induced oscillation [Ca2+]I signals in human sperm.

the role of Ca2+-ATPas in spermatozoa.
the mechanisms that underpin Ca2+ signalling in spermatozoa and how they are modulated by physiological and pharmacological agents.
the mechanisms that control intracellular Ca2 + signalling in human spermatoza and its relevance to the regulation of human spermatozoal function.

the Ca2+ pumps that are involved in the regulation of Ca2+ oscillations in sperm are not SERCAs.
